desc: Shenzhen warehouse automation company making autonomous case-handling robots and HaiPick systems that lift totes and cartons for e-commerce and retail.

rationale: B2B robotics brand with no consumer awareness; automation technology offers a showcase for logistics customers, but F1 fit is modest.

name: Klöckner Pentaplast
desc: Maker of rigid and flexible plastic films and packaging for pharmaceutical, food and medical customers, with plants in 18 countries.
markets: Plants in about 18 countries supplying drugmakers and food producers; Crunchbase shows London although the group is usually associated with Montabaur, Germany.
rationale: B2B packaging supplier with no consumer brand awareness and a debt restructuring in 2024; weak F1 fit.
changed: Restructured its debt in 2024, giving lenders control

name: Korea Zinc
desc: South Korean non-ferrous metals producer and the world's largest zinc smelter, also making lead, silver, gold and copper.
markets: Smelter at Onsan in South Korea, Sun Metals in Australia and a Peruvian subsidiary; sells metals to industrial customers worldwide.
rationale: B2B metals brand with no consumer profile; a 2024-25 shareholder control dispute also makes a sponsorship deal unlikely.
changed: Control contest between the Choi family and Young Poong with MBK Partners from 2024

name: Changxin New Bridge
desc: Chinese industrial manufacturer that Crunchbase says produces industrial goods; its products, customers and ownership are not confirmed.
markets: Only a Chinese location is supported; customers, scale and markets are unconfirmed.
rationale: Unverified industrial manufacturer with no known brand or international activity; weak F1 fit.

name: Berry Global
desc: Plastic packaging maker supplying containers, closures, films, nonwovens and healthcare products to consumer goods, food and industrial customers.
markets: Plants worldwide supplying consumer goods, food and industrial customers; merged into Amcor in 2025.
rationale: B2B packaging supplier now inside Amcor; brand awareness is low and any F1 deal would sit with the parent.
changed: Merged with Amcor in 2025

name: DOF
desc: Norwegian subsea and offshore marine services company operating construction and support vessels for oil, gas and offshore wind customers.
markets: Operates in the North Sea, Brazil and other regions for energy majors such as Petrobras and Equinor.
rationale: B2B offshore services firm with no consumer brand awareness; hospitality for energy customers is possible, but fit is weak.

name: Koppers
desc: Integrated provider of treated wood products, wood treatment chemicals and carbon compounds such as carbon pitch for aluminium production.
markets: Customers include railroads, utilities, lumber retailers and industrial users in North America, Europe, Australia and Asia.
rationale: B2B industrial brand with limited consumer awareness and little international marketing activity; F1 fit is weak.

name: Nordson
desc: Precision technology company making dispensing, coating, fluid control and testing equipment, plus medical and electronics inspection systems.
markets: Sells to packaging, consumer goods, medical device and electronics manufacturers in more than 35 countries.
rationale: B2B industrial equipment brand with no consumer awareness; F1 offers a precision-engineering showcase and customer hospitality, but fit is modest.

name: Parkland
desc: Canadian fuel distributor and convenience store operator with retail brands including Chevron, Ultramar, Pioneer and On the Run.
markets: Retail fuel and convenience stores across Canada, plus fuel supply in the US and the Caribbean; agreed in 2025 to be acquired by Sunoco LP.
rationale: Highly visible Canadian fuel retail brand with consumer reach, but now being absorbed by Sunoco; Montreal and Canadian race promotion could fit.
changed: Agreed in 2025 to be acquired by Sunoco LP

name: Valmet
desc: Finnish supplier of technologies, automation and services for pulp, paper, board and energy industries, selling process equipment and service contracts.
markets: Serves mills and energy producers worldwide; spun off from Metso in 2013.
rationale: B2B industrial brand with no consumer awareness; F1 offers customer hospitality and an automation technology showcase, but fit is modest.
changed: Spun off from Metso in 2013

name: ADNOC Drilling
desc: Drilling arm of the Abu Dhabi National Oil Company, operating onshore and offshore rigs and integrated drilling services.
markets: Main customer is ADNOC in the Middle East; has expanded into the US through joint ventures and acquisitions.
rationale: B2B drilling contractor with a state-owned parent and no consumer brand; the parent's Gulf profile gives some hospitality angle but little direct use.

name: Allegro MicroSystems
desc: Semiconductor company making magnetic sensors and power ICs for electric vehicles, driver assistance, industrial automation and data centres.
markets: Operations in the US, Philippines and Thailand; sells to automakers and industrial manufacturers worldwide.
rationale: B2B chip supplier with no consumer brand; automotive and electrification technology gives a link to F1, but marketing scale is modest.

name: SK Siltron CSS
desc: Silicon carbide wafer business of SK Siltron making substrates and epitaxial wafers for electric vehicle power electronics, chargers and inverters.
markets: Production in Michigan supplying power chip manufacturers; acquired from DuPont in 2020 and part of South Korea's SK Group.
rationale: B2B wafer supplier with no consumer awareness; EV power technology gives a loose F1 link but little marketing use.
changed: Acquired from DuPont by SK Siltron in 2020

name: Carbon
desc: 3D printing company whose Digital Light Synthesis technology produces polymer parts for manufacturers, selling printers on subscription plus resins.
markets: Customers include adidas for running shoe midsoles, dental labs, automotive and medical device firms; sells to manufacturers in several regions.
rationale: 3D printing is already a theme in F1 through rivals 3D Systems and Stratasys, and adidas is a customer, giving a clear technology showcase.

name: Cascades
desc: Quebec manufacturer of tissue, containerboard and packaging products from recycled fibre for consumers and the away-from-home market.
markets: Sells in Canada and the US with branded tissue lines and Cascades Pro.
rationale: Mostly B2B and private-label focused with a regional consumer presence; sustainability angle exists, but F1 fit is weak.

name: Meitu
desc: Chinese consumer app company known for Meitu Xiu Xiu, BeautyCam and the Wink video editor, earning subscription and advertising revenue.
markets: Strong in China and parts of Asia with hundreds of millions of monthly users; reach outside Asia is not confirmed.
rationale: Consumer app brand with a young, social audience; F1 offers fan reach, though its main markets are China and Asia.

name: Aalberts
desc: Dutch industrial technology group making piping systems, valves, surface treatments and precision parts for building, industrial and semiconductor customers.
markets: Sells to installers, wholesalers and manufacturers in over 50 countries.
rationale: B2B industrial brand with trade recognition but little consumer awareness; F1 offers customer hospitality and an engineering showcase, with modest fit.

name: Canadian Utilities
desc: Alberta energy infrastructure company operating regulated electricity transmission and distribution, natural gas distribution, pipelines, storage and power generation.
markets: Serves about 1.5 million customers, mainly in Alberta; part of the ATCO group.
rationale: Regulated utility with local consumer visibility and no international growth story; F1 fit is weak.

name: POSCO International
desc: Korean trading and energy company handling steel, food, mobility parts and energy, with LNG and an EV motor-core business.
markets: Trades and operates in many countries, including Myanmar gas fields; part of POSCO Group.
rationale: B2B trading brand with moderate corporate awareness in Korea; EV motor cores give a loose F1 link, but consumer fit is weak.

name: Belden
desc: Manufacturer of signal transmission, networking and connectivity products and cable for industrial, enterprise and broadband customers, including Hirschmann and Lumberg.
markets: Sells industrial networking, broadband and enterprise connectivity products to customers in North America, Europe and Asia.
rationale: B2B networking supplier with little consumer awareness; F1 offers a connectivity showcase and customer hospitality, but fit is modest.

name: Panavision
desc: Designer and manufacturer of high-precision cameras and lenses for film and television, with a major equipment rental business for studios.
markets: Customers are studios and cinematographers; known in the film industry, with limited consumer awareness.
rationale: Respected film technology brand; F1 content and broadcast storytelling give a creative showcase, but it is a niche B2B name.

name: Meshy AI
desc: AI platform turning text and images into 3D models, textures and animations for game developers, designers and 3D printing users.
markets: Sold online to users reportedly numbering millions; specific countries are not confirmed, and the funding figure shown looks unreliable.
rationale: Rising creative AI brand with a young developer audience; F1 offers a technology showcase, but the company is early and budget is uncertain.

name: The Elmet Group
desc: Manufacturer of precision tungsten and molybdenum products such as wire, sheets and components for aerospace, lighting, medical and semiconductor industries.
markets: US-based specialty manufacturer serving industrial customers; international sales and ownership are not confirmed.
rationale: Small B2B specialty manufacturer with no consumer recognition and no known international marketing activity; weak F1 fit.

name: Velo3D
desc: Metal 3D printing company selling Sapphire laser powder bed fusion printers and software for aerospace, defence and energy parts.
markets: Customers include SpaceX and other aerospace firms; went public via a SPAC in 2021, was delisted and later relisted after restructuring.
rationale: Metal 3D printing is already an F1 theme through rivals 3D Systems and Stratasys, but finances have been strained and brand awareness is limited.
changed: Listed via SPAC in 2021; delisted and later relisted on Nasdaq after restructuring

name: Unitree Robotics
desc: Hangzhou maker of Go2 and B2 quadruped robot dogs and H1 and G1 humanoid robots for research, entertainment and industry.
markets: Sells robots to research, entertainment and industrial buyers in China and abroad; was reported to be preparing a STAR Market listing.
rationale: Viral consumer-facing robotics brand with a strong technology image; F1 could suit a showcase for Chinese and global tech audiences.

name: HEXO
desc: Canadian cannabis producer selling to adult consumers under brands including Hexo, Up and Original Stash, now part of Tilray.
markets: Sold in Canada only; no longer an independent company after being absorbed by Tilray.
rationale: Cannabis advertising is restricted and the company is no longer independent; F1 sponsorship is effectively unavailable.
changed: Acquired by Tilray in 2023 and delisted

name: Endesa
desc: Spain's largest electricity utility generating, distributing and selling electricity and gas to about 10 million customers in Spain and Portugal.
markets: Customers in Spain and Portugal; majority owned by Italy's Enel, with a mix of nuclear, renewable and gas generation.
rationale: Strong consumer-facing energy brand in Iberia with sport sponsorship history; Spanish Grand Prix hosting and electrification messaging fit, though its market is only Iberia.

name: DFD
desc: High-tech manufacturing enterprise in Jiaozuo, Henan, engaged in research, development and production; its products and customers are not confirmed.
markets: Only a Jiaozuo, Henan location is supported; customers and markets are unconfirmed, and the name is ambiguous.
rationale: Unverified manufacturer with no known brand or international activity; F1 fit cannot be judged and appears weak.

name: Kingboard Holdings
desc: Hong Kong group whose companies make copper-clad laminates, printed circuit boards and chemicals for electronics manufacturers.
markets: Sells laminates and circuit boards to electronics manufacturers; Kingboard Laminates is among the world's largest laminate makers.
rationale: B2B electronics materials group with no consumer brand; F1 offers little beyond customer hospitality.

name: ATS Corporation
desc: Canadian builder of custom automation systems, such as assembly and test lines, for life sciences, transportation and food customers.
markets: Serves customers in North America, Europe and Asia with custom-engineered automation.
rationale: B2B engineering brand with no consumer recognition; F1 offers an automation and precision showcase plus customer hospitality, but fit is modest.

name: IMA Group
desc: Italian maker of automatic machines for packaging pharmaceuticals, tea, coffee and cosmetics, selling to drug, food and beverage companies.
markets: Sells to pharmaceutical, food and beverage customers worldwide; controlled by Alberto Vacchi and BC Partners since 2020.
rationale: B2B machine builder with no consumer awareness; Italian engineering heritage and Italian races offer customer hospitality, but fit is modest.
changed: BC Partners bought a major stake in 2020

name: MasterBrand
desc: Largest North American maker of kitchen and bath cabinets, with brands including Diamond, Omega and Schrock, sold through home centres.
markets: Sells to homeowners and builders in North America; spun off from Fortune Brands in 2022 and bought Supreme Cabinetry in 2024.
rationale: Home-improvement brand with US consumer recognition; US Grand Prix hospitality for dealers and builders is possible, but it is a North American business.
changed: Spun off from Fortune Brands in 2022

name: Greenview Fertiliser
desc: Holding company for Dangote group fertiliser operations in Nigeria, according to its Crunchbase description.
markets: Linked to Dangote fertiliser operations in Nigeria; location data in the line is garbled, and exports are not confirmed.
rationale: Holding vehicle with little standalone consumer visibility; any marketing would sit with the Dangote group, so direct F1 fit is weak.

name: Nordic Paper
desc: Swedish maker of greaseproof and kraft paper for food packaging, baking paper and industrial uses, with Nordic mills.
markets: Mills in Sweden and Norway supplying converters and packaging manufacturers, mainly in Europe; ownership has not been re-verified.
rationale: Commodity B2B paper producer with no consumer brand and a mainly European customer base; weak F1 fit.

name: Stryten Energy
desc: US maker of lead-acid and lithium batteries and energy storage systems for submarines, military vehicles, motive power, telecom and utilities.
markets: US plants serving defence, industrial, telecom and utility customers; ownership and international sales are not confirmed.
rationale: B2B battery maker with low consumer awareness and defence exposure; energy storage offers a loose technology link to F1.

name: Loscam
desc: Pallet and returnable packaging pooling company renting wooden and plastic pallets and containers to manufacturers, FMCG suppliers and retailers.
markets: Depots across Asia Pacific including Australia, New Zealand, China, Vietnam, Thailand and Malaysia; originated in Australia.
rationale: B2B logistics asset provider with low consumer awareness; hospitality for FMCG customers in Asia Pacific is possible, but fit is weak.

name: John Cockerill Hydrogen
desc: Belgian maker of alkaline water electrolyzers for green hydrogen production, selling systems and stacks to energy and industry project developers.
markets: Manufacturing in Belgium, France and China, selling to project developers worldwide; part of the John Cockerill Group.
rationale: Hydrogen technology fits F1 sustainability messaging and a Belgian Grand Prix link, but it is a B2B brand with little consumer awareness.

name: Exail Technologies
desc: French group making navigation systems, inertial sensors, autonomous vessels, underwater drones and photonics for defence, marine, space and aviation customers.
markets: Defence and civil marine customers in several regions; formed in 2022 when iXblue merged with ECA Group.
rationale: B2B defence and marine technology brand with little consumer awareness; naval focus makes F1 sponsorship unlikely.
changed: iXblue merged with ECA Group in 2022
